newsitem.title: UK: London gold sleepy ahead of IMF gold sale meeting.
newsitem.headline: London gold sleepy ahead of IMF gold sale meeting.

text.p: Gold prices were lower and business extremely thin on Wednesday ahead of an International Monetary Fund (IMF) meeting on possible gold sales, dealers said.
"All the precious metals are sleeping. Gold hasn't moved all morning," a dealer said. "There is just no interest."
Bullion fixed at $382.90 an ounce, compared to $383.45 on Tuesday afternoon and $383.30 in the morning. Prices dropped modestly in New York late on Tuesday.
Fresh demand from jewellery manufacturers, boosted by the approach of the Indian festival season, was keeping gold prices above the $382 support area.
But selling by gold miners was expected to apply downside pressure if prices rose to around $385.
The market would be watching closely for the outcome of an IMF meeting later on Wednesday on a proposal to sell five million ounces of gold to help finance aid to poor countries.
But a number of dealers said they doubted that a decision, if taken, would produce much drama in the market.
"It's already been discounted," a dealer said, adding that the volume of gold in question was too small to have a significant effect on the bullion market.
Fresh U.S. interest rate jitters were also seen having minimal immediate effect on gold.
A surge and subsequent easing of European and U.S. stock markets earlier this week had elicited little reaction in the precious metals.
Silver, which has been following gold, was one cent firmer compared to Tuesday's London close at $5.06 an ounce.
Platinum was slightly weaker at $388.00, down $0.75.
Palladium, which had fixed at a three-year low on Tuesday, was still lower at $120.75. It shed $1.00 from Tuesday's London close and was vulnerable to further losses, dealers said.
